## CFTC Regulation 1.31 — Regulatory records; retention and production

Retention periods, form and manner of retention (authenticity, reliability, system inventory) and inspection and production duties for CFTC regulatory records.

- **Citation:** [17 CFR 1.31](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-1.31) (Commodity Futures Trading Commission)
- **Status:** in force as of 2026-09-16
- **Applies to:** Any person required by the Commodity Exchange Act or CFTC regulations to keep regulatory records
- **Cloud relevance:** high
- **Confidence:** high. Verified 2026-09-18 by claude-opus-5 agent session (not reviewed by counsel). Read the current primary text retrieved from the official publisher; every quoted obligation was compared against it verbatim.
- **Review due:** 2027-03-18

<a id="us-cftc-1-31-b1"></a>

### Swap records kept five years after the transaction ends

`us-cftc-1-31.b1` · retention · applies to CFTC records entities holding records of swaps or related cash or forward transactions

Keep regulatory records of each swap or related cash or forward transaction from creation until the transaction terminates, matures, expires, or is transferred, assigned or novated, and for at least five years after that.

- **Retention:** **5 years**. Trigger: Termination, maturity, expiration, transfer, assignment or novation date of the transaction
- **Source:** [17 CFR 1.31(b)(1)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-1.31#p-1.31(b)(1)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (1) A records entity shall keep regulatory records of any swap or related cash or forward transaction (as defined in § 23.200(i) of this chapter), other than regulatory records required by § 23.202(a)(1) and (b)(1)-(3) of this chapter, from the date the regulatory record was created until the termination, maturity, expiration, transfer, assignment, or novation date of the transaction and for a period of not less than five years after such date.

<a id="us-cftc-1-31-b2"></a>

### Oral communications kept one year

`us-cftc-1-31.b2` · retention · applies to CFTC records entities required to retain oral communications

Keep regulatory records of oral communications for at least one year from the date of the communication.

- **Retention:** **1 year**. Trigger: Date of the communication
- **Source:** [17 CFR 1.31(b)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-1.31#p-1.31(b)(2)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-communications-capture](#ctl-communications-capture), [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (2) A records entity that is required to retain oral communications, shall keep regulatory records of oral communications for a period of not less than one year from the date of such communication.

<a id="us-cftc-1-31-b3"></a>

### All other regulatory records kept five years from creation

`us-cftc-1-31.b3` · retention · applies to CFTC records entities

Keep every other regulatory record for at least five years from the date it was created.

- **Retention:** **5 years**. Trigger: Date the record was created
- **Source:** [17 CFR 1.31(b)(3)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-1.31#p-1.31(b)(3)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (3) A records entity shall keep each regulatory record other than the records described in paragraphs (b)(1) or (b)(2) of this section for a period of not less than five years from the date on which the record was created.

<a id="us-cftc-1-31-b4"></a>

### Electronic records readily accessible for the whole retention period

`us-cftc-1-31.b4` · retention · applies to CFTC records entities

Keep paper-only regulatory records readily accessible for at least two years, and electronic regulatory records readily accessible for the whole required period.

- **Retention:** **Accessibility window only**; readily accessible for the first 2 years. Trigger: Paper-only records are readily accessible for the stated window; electronic records stay readily accessible for their full retention period.
- **Source:** [17 CFR 1.31(b)(4)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-1.31#p-1.31(b)(4)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (4) A records entity shall keep regulatory records exclusively created and maintained on paper readily accessible for no less than two years. A records entity shall keep electronic regulatory records readily accessible for the duration of the required record keeping period.

<a id="us-cftc-1-31-c2"></a>

### Systems and controls for authentic, reliable, available electronic records, plus a system inventory

`us-cftc-1-31.c2` · form · applies to CFTC records entities maintaining electronic regulatory records

Establish systems that preserve the security, signature and data of electronic records, ensure they can be produced and stay available through a disruption, and keep an up-to-date inventory of every system needed to access or produce them.

- **Source:** [17 CFR 1.31(c)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-1.31#p-1.31(c)(2)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-access-restriction](#ctl-access-restriction), [ctl-audit-trail](#ctl-audit-trail), [ctl-integrity-verification](#ctl-integrity-verification), [ctl-records-register](#ctl-records-register), [ctl-redundant-copy](#ctl-redundant-copy), [ctl-worm-storage](#ctl-worm-storage)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (2) Electronic regulatory records. Each records entity maintaining electronic regulatory records shall establish appropriate systems and controls that ensure the authenticity and reliability of electronic regulatory records, including, without limitation: [...] (ii) Systems that ensure the records entity is able to produce electronic regulatory records in accordance with this section, and ensure the availability of such regulatory records in the event of an emergency or other disruption of the records entity's electronic record retention systems; and (iii) The creation and maintenance of an up-to-date inventory that identifies and describes each system that maintains information necessary for accessing or producing electronic regulatory records.

<a id="us-cftc-1-31-d3"></a>

### Produce electronic records promptly in the form and medium requested

`us-cftc-1-31.d3` · production · applies to CFTC records entities

Produce electronic regulatory records promptly, in the reasonable form and medium a Commission representative specifies.

- **Source:** [17 CFR 1.31(d)(3)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-1.31#p-1.31(d)(3)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-regulator-production](#ctl-regulator-production)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (ii) A records entity must produce such regulatory records in the form and medium requested promptly, upon request, unless otherwise directed by the Commission representative.

## FINRA Rule 4511 — General Requirements (books and records)

Requires members to make and preserve books and records, sets a default retention period where no other rule specifies one, and requires the Rule 17a-4 format and media.

- **Citation:** [FINRA Rule 4511](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/rulebooks/finra-rules/4511) (Financial Industry Regulatory Authority)
- **Status:** in force as of 2026-09-18
- **Applies to:** FINRA member firms
- **Cloud relevance:** high
- **Confidence:** high. Verified 2026-09-18 by claude-opus-5 agent session (not reviewed by counsel). Read the current primary text retrieved from the official publisher; every quoted obligation was compared against it verbatim.
- **Review due:** 2027-03-18

<a id="us-finra-4511-a"></a>

### Make and preserve books and records required by FINRA and Exchange Act rules

`us-finra-4511.a` · creation · applies to FINRA member firms

Make and preserve the books and records required by FINRA rules, the Exchange Act and the applicable Exchange Act rules.

- **Source:** [FINRA Rule 4511(a)](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/rulebooks/finra-rules/4511), retrieved 2026-09-18
- **See also:** `us-sec-17a-3.a`
- **Controls:** [ctl-records-register](#ctl-records-register)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (a) Members shall make and preserve books and records as required under the FINRA rules, the Exchange Act and the applicable Exchange Act rules.

<a id="us-finra-4511-b"></a>

### Six-year default retention where no other period is specified

`us-finra-4511.b` · retention · applies to FINRA member firms

Preserve FINRA books and records that have no period specified in FINRA rules or applicable Exchange Act rules for at least six years.

- **Retention:** **6 years**. Trigger: The rule states the period without naming its start.
- **Source:** [FINRA Rule 4511(b)](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/rulebooks/finra-rules/4511), retrieved 2026-09-18
- **Controls:** [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (b) Members shall preserve for a period of at least six years those FINRA books and records for which there is no specified period under the FINRA rules or applicable Exchange Act rules.

<a id="us-finra-4511-c"></a>

### Preserve in a format and media that complies with SEA Rule 17a-4

`us-finra-4511.c` · form · applies to FINRA member firms

Preserve records required by FINRA rules in a format and media that complies with SEA Rule 17a-4.

- **Source:** [FINRA Rule 4511(c)](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/rulebooks/finra-rules/4511), retrieved 2026-09-18
- **See also:** `us-sec-17a-4.f2i`
- **Controls:** [ctl-worm-storage](#ctl-worm-storage)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (c) All books and records required to be made pursuant to the FINRA rules shall be preserved in a format and media that complies with SEA Rule 17a-4.

## SEC Rule 17a-3 — Records to be made by certain exchange members, brokers and dealers

Defines which books and records a broker-dealer must create and keep current. It sets no retention periods; those are in Rule 17a-4.

- **Citation:** [17 CFR 240.17a-3](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-3) (Securities and Exchange Commission)
- **Status:** in force as of 2026-09-16
- **Applies to:** Exchange members, brokers and dealers registered under section 15 of the Exchange Act
- **Cloud relevance:** high
- **Confidence:** high. Verified 2026-09-18 by claude-opus-5 agent session (not reviewed by counsel). Read the current primary text retrieved from the official publisher; every quoted obligation was compared against it verbatim.
- **Review due:** 2027-03-18

<a id="us-sec-17a-3-a"></a>

### Make and keep current the required books and records

`us-sec-17a-3.a` · creation · applies to Exchange members, brokers and dealers

Create each book and record listed in paragraph (a) of the rule and keep it current. Retention periods are set by the preservation rule; see the linked obligations.

- **Source:** [17 CFR 240.17a-3(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-3#p-240.17a-3(a)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **See also:** `us-sec-17a-4.a`, `us-sec-17a-4.b`
- **Controls:** [ctl-records-register](#ctl-records-register)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> Every member of a national securities exchange who transacts a business in securities directly with others than members of a national securities exchange, every broker or dealer who transacts a business in securities through the medium of any such member, and every broker or dealer registered pursuant to section 15 of the Act (15 U.S.C. 78o) must make and keep current the following books and records relating to its business:

<a id="us-sec-17a-3-a6"></a>

### Order memoranda with time of receipt, entry and execution

`us-sec-17a-3.a6` · creation · applies to Exchange members, brokers and dealers

Keep a memorandum of every brokerage order or instruction, whether executed or not, showing its terms, the account, when it was received and entered, the execution price, who handled it, and where feasible when it was executed or cancelled.

- **Source:** [17 CFR 240.17a-3(a)(6)(i)(A)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-3#p-240.17a-3(a)(6)(i)(A)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **See also:** `us-sec-17a-4.b`
- **Controls:** [ctl-records-register](#ctl-records-register)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> The memorandum must show the terms and conditions of the order or instructions and of any modification or cancellation thereof, the account for which entered, the time the order was received, the time of entry, the price at which executed, the identity of each associated person, if any, responsible for the account, the identity of any other person who entered or accepted the order on behalf of the customer, or, if a customer entered the order on an electronic system, a notation of that entry; and, to the extent feasible, the time of execution or cancellation.

## SEC Rule 17a-4 — Records to be preserved by certain exchange members, brokers and dealers

Retention periods, electronic recordkeeping system requirements (audit-trail or non-rewriteable, non-erasable storage), third-party recordkeeper undertakings and production duties for broker-dealer records.

- **Citation:** [17 CFR 240.17a-4](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-4) (Securities and Exchange Commission)
- **Status:** in force as of 2026-09-16
- **Applies to:** Exchange members, brokers and dealers subject to Rule 17a-3
- **Cloud relevance:** high
- **Confidence:** high. Verified 2026-09-18 by claude-opus-5 agent session (not reviewed by counsel). Read the current primary text retrieved from the official publisher; every quoted obligation was compared against it verbatim.
- **Review due:** 2027-03-18

<a id="us-sec-17a-4-a"></a>

### Six-year retention for blotters, ledgers and core records

`us-sec-17a-4.a` · retention · applies to Members, brokers and dealers subject to Rule 17a-3

Preserve the records made under Rule 17a-3(a)(1)-(3), (5), (21) and (22) for at least 6 years, the first two years in an easily accessible place.

- **Retention:** **6 years**; readily accessible for the first 2 years. Trigger: The rule states the period without naming its start; firms conventionally run it from the record's creation.
- **Source:** [17 CFR 240.17a-4(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-4#p-240.17a-4(a)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (a) Every member, broker or dealer subject to § 240.17a-3 must preserve for a period of not less than 6 years, the first two years in an easily accessible place, all records required to be made pursuant to § 240.17a-3(a)(1) through (3), (5), and (21) and (22), and analogous records created pursuant to § 240.17a-3(e).

<a id="us-sec-17a-4-b"></a>

### Three-year retention for other records, including business communications

`us-sec-17a-4.b` · retention · applies to Members, brokers and dealers subject to Rule 17a-3

Preserve the paragraph (b) records for at least three years, the first two in an easily accessible place. They include bank records, trial balances, written agreements, and originals or copies of all business communications sent and received.

- **Retention:** **3 years**; readily accessible for the first 2 years. Trigger: The rule states the period without naming its start; firms conventionally run it from the record's creation.
- **Source:** [17 CFR 240.17a-4(b), (b)(4)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-4#p-240.17a-4(b)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-communications-capture](#ctl-communications-capture), [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (b) Every member, broker or dealer subject to § 240.17a-3 must preserve for a period of not less than three years, the first two years in an easily accessible place: [...] (4) Originals of all communications received and copies of all communications sent (and any approvals thereof) by the member, broker or dealer (including inter-office memoranda and communications) relating to its business as such

<a id="us-sec-17a-4-c"></a>

### Account-opening records kept six years after the account closes

`us-sec-17a-4.c` · retention · applies to Members, brokers and dealers subject to Rule 17a-3

Preserve account cards or records on the terms of opening and maintaining a customer account until at least six years after the account closes.

- **Retention:** **6 years**. Trigger: Closing of the customer's account
- **Source:** [17 CFR 240.17a-4(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-4#p-240.17a-4(c)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (c) Every member, broker or dealer subject to § 240.17a-3 must preserve for a period of not less than six years after the closing of any customer's account any account cards or records which relate to the terms and conditions with respect to the opening and maintenance of the account.

<a id="us-sec-17a-4-d"></a>

### Constitutional and registration records kept for the life of the enterprise

`us-sec-17a-4.d` · retention · applies to Members, brokers and dealers subject to Rule 17a-3

Preserve partnership articles or articles of incorporation, minute books, stock certificate books and registration forms for the life of the enterprise and any successor.

- **Retention:** **Indefinite**. Trigger: Life of the enterprise and of any successor enterprise
- **Source:** [17 CFR 240.17a-4(d)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-4#p-240.17a-4(d)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-indefinite-and-legal-hold](#ctl-indefinite-and-legal-hold)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (d) Every member, broker or dealer subject to § 240.17a-3 must preserve during the life of the enterprise and of any successor enterprise all partnership articles or, in the case of a corporation, all articles of incorporation or charter, minute books, and stock certificate books

<a id="us-sec-17a-4-f2i"></a>

### Electronic records need a complete audit trail or non-rewriteable, non-erasable storage

`us-sec-17a-4.f2i` · form · applies to Broker-dealers keeping required records on an electronic recordkeeping system

For the whole retention period, either keep a complete time-stamped audit trail of every modification and deletion that allows the original record to be re-created, or store the records exclusively in non-rewriteable, non-erasable (WORM) form.

- **Source:** [17 CFR 240.17a-4(f)(2)(i)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-4#p-240.17a-4(f)(2)(i)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-audit-trail](#ctl-audit-trail), [ctl-worm-storage](#ctl-worm-storage)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (i)(A) Preserve a record for the duration of its applicable retention period in a manner that maintains a complete time-stamped audit trail that includes: [...] (4) Any other information needed to maintain an audit trail of the record in a way that maintains security, signatures, and data to ensure the authenticity and reliability of the record and will permit re-creation of the original record if it is modified or deleted; or (B) Preserve the records exclusively in a non-rewriteable, non-erasable format;

<a id="us-sec-17a-4-f2ii"></a>

### Automatic verification of storage completeness and accuracy

`us-sec-17a-4.f2ii` · form · applies to Broker-dealers keeping required records on an electronic recordkeeping system

The system must automatically verify that the processes for storing and retaining records electronically are complete and accurate.

- **Source:** [17 CFR 240.17a-4(f)(2)(ii)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.17a-4#p-240.17a-4(f)(2)(ii)), retrieved 2026-09-18 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16)
- **Controls:** [ctl-integrity-verification](#ctl-integrity-verification)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

<a id="us-sec-17a-4-f2v"></a>

### Backup recordkeeping system or equivalent redundancy

`us-sec-17a-4.f2v` · form · applies to Broker-dealers keeping required records on an electronic recordkeeping system

Keep a backup electronic recordkeeping system that meets the same requirements and can serve as a redundant set of records, or have other redundancy that ensures access to the records.

`us-sec-17a-4.f3iv` · production · applies to Broker-dealers using an electronic recordkeeping system

### Undertaking from a third-party recordkeeper, including a cloud provider

`us-sec-17a-4.i` · undertaking · applies to Broker-dealers whose records are held by an outside service, including one that owns and operates the storage servers

When an outside entity prepares or keeps the records, including one that owns the storage servers, it must file a written undertaking with the Commission. If the broker-dealer has independent access to the records, a shorter undertaking in which the outside entity agrees not to impede examination may be filed instead.

## SEC Rule 204-2 — Books and records to be maintained by investment advisers

Which books and records an investment adviser must keep, how long, and the conditions for keeping them on micrographic or electronic storage media.

- **Status:** in force as of 2026-09-16
- **Applies to:** Investment advisers registered or required to be registered under section 203 of the Advisers Act
- **Cloud relevance:** high
- **Confidence:** high. Verified 2026-09-18 by claude-opus-5 agent session (not reviewed by counsel). Read the current primary text retrieved from the official publisher; every quoted obligation was compared against it verbatim.

<a id="us-sec-204-2-e1"></a>

### Five-year retention from the end of the fiscal year of the last entry

`us-sec-204-2.e1` · retention · applies to Registered investment advisers

<a id="us-sox-802"></a>

## Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, Section 802 — Criminal penalties for altering documents

Makes destroying or altering records to obstruct a federal matter a crime, and requires auditors to retain audit workpapers. SEC Rule 2-06 implements the workpaper retention.

- **Citation:** [Pub. L. 107-204, title VIII, §802 (18 U.S.C. 1519, 1520)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-107publ204/html/PLAW-107publ204.htm) (U.S. Congress)
- **Status:** in force as of 2026-09-18
- **Applies to:** Anyone, for 18 U.S.C. 1519. Accountants auditing issuers, for 18 U.S.C. 1520 and SEC Rule 2-06.
- **Cloud relevance:** medium
- **Confidence:** high. Verified 2026-09-18 by claude-opus-5 agent session (not reviewed by counsel). Read the current primary text retrieved from the official publisher; every quoted obligation was compared against it verbatim.
- **Review due:** 2027-03-18

<a id="us-sox-802-1519"></a>

### Do not destroy, alter or falsify records to obstruct a federal matter

`us-sox-802.1519` · preservation · applies to Any person

Do not knowingly destroy, alter, conceal or falsify any record with intent to obstruct a federal investigation or bankruptcy case, including one only contemplated. The penalty is imprisonment of up to 20 years. In practice this means suspending routine deletion under a legal hold once such a matter is reasonably anticipated.

- **Source:** [18 U.S.C. 1519 (added by SOX §802(a))](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title18-section1519&num=0&edition=prelim), retrieved 2026-09-18 (U.S. Code, prelim edition as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel)
- **Controls:** [ctl-indefinite-and-legal-hold](#ctl-indefinite-and-legal-hold)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> Whoever knowingly alters, destroys, mutilates, conceals, covers up, falsifies, or makes a false entry in any record, document, or tangible object with the intent to impede, obstruct, or influence the investigation or proper administration of any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the United States or any case filed under title 11, or in relation to or contemplation of any such matter or case, shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than 20 years, or both.

<a id="us-sox-802-1520"></a>

### Auditors retain audit and review workpapers five years (statutory floor)

`us-sox-802.1520` · retention · applies to Accountants auditing issuers under section 10A(a) of the Exchange Act

Keep all audit or review workpapers for five years from the end of the fiscal period in which the audit or review concluded. SEC Rule 2-06 extends this.

- **Retention:** **5 years**. Trigger: End of the fiscal period in which the audit or review was concluded
- **Source:** [18 U.S.C. 1520(a)(1)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title18-section1520&num=0&edition=prelim), retrieved 2026-09-18 (U.S. Code, prelim edition as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel)
- **See also:** `us-sox-802.rule2-06`
- **Controls:** [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** high; review due 2027-03-18

> (a)(1) Any accountant who conducts an audit of an issuer of securities to which section 10A(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78j–1(a)) applies, shall maintain all audit or review workpapers for a period of 5 years from the end of the fiscal period in which the audit or review was concluded.

Keep workpapers and other records relevant to the audit or review, including correspondence and electronic records containing conclusions, opinions, analyses or financial data, for seven years after the audit or review concludes.

## Controls

<a id="ctl-access-restriction"></a>

### Least-privilege access to records, with dedicated keys

`ctl-access-restriction` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Restrict access to the records buckets to named roles for authorized personnel and regulator-access procedures. Encrypt with customer-managed KMS keys whose key policies name the same roles. Log every access through the audit trail.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-204-2.g3`](#us-sec-204-2-g3), [`us-cftc-1-31.c2`](#us-cftc-1-31-c2)
- **Evidence:**
  - IAM and bucket policies for the records buckets, with periodic access reviews
  - KMS key policies and key usage logs
- **AWS:**
  - [AWS IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html): Role-based least privilege scoped to records buckets
  - [AWS KMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/overview.html): Customer-managed keys per records domain

<a id="ctl-audit-trail"></a>

### Tamper-evident audit trail of record creation, modification and deletion

`ctl-audit-trail` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Log S3 data events for every records bucket to a CloudTrail trail with log file integrity validation. Keep the trail in an Object Lock bucket in a separate log-archive account. Versioning on the records buckets keeps prior content, so a modified record can be re-created. This combination is what the 17a-4(f)(2)(i)(A) audit-trail alternative requires. Firms that choose the WORM option still need an input audit system under 17a-4(f)(3)(iii), and this trail provides it.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-4.f2i`](#us-sec-17a-4-f2i), [`us-cftc-1-31.c2`](#us-cftc-1-31-c2)
- **Evidence:**
  - CloudTrail trail configuration with data events on the records buckets and LogFileValidationEnabled true
  - Periodic output of validate-logs showing the digest chain intact
  - Log-archive bucket Object Lock configuration
- **AWS:**
  - [AWS CloudTrail (data events, log file integrity validation)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-log-file-validation-intro.html): Organization trail, S3 data events for records buckets, log file validation on, delivered to a locked log-archive bucket
  - [AWS CloudTrail Lake](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.html): Event data store for queryable retention of the same events
- **Limits:** CloudTrail records API actions, not business-level edits made inside an application database. An application that changes records before writing them to S3 needs its own audit trail.

<a id="ctl-communications-capture"></a>

### Capture and retain business communications and recorded calls

`ctl-communications-capture` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Route every approved business communication channel (email, chat, recorded telephony) to capture that writes into the WORM records buckets under the communications retention class. For telephony on Amazon Connect, send call recordings to a locked bucket. Channels that cannot be captured are prohibited for business use, mirroring the Article 16(7) duty to prevent unrecordable communications on private equipment.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-4.b`](#us-sec-17a-4-b), [`us-cftc-1-31.b2`](#us-cftc-1-31-b2)
- **Evidence:**
  - Channel inventory showing the capture path for each approved channel
  - Connect instance storage configuration pointing recordings at the locked bucket
  - Surveillance sampling reports that confirm capture completeness
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon Connect call recording](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/set-up-recordings.html): Recordings delivered to an Object Lock bucket under the communications retention class
- **Limits:** Capturing third-party messaging apps needs vendor archiving connectors, which are outside this corpus.

<a id="ctl-indefinite-and-legal-hold"></a>

### Legal holds for indefinite retention and anticipated investigations

`ctl-indefinite-and-legal-hold` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Place an Object Lock legal hold on life-of-enterprise records (charter documents, minute books, registration forms), because a legal hold has no expiry date. Keep a documented legal-hold procedure. When a federal investigation or proceeding is reasonably anticipated, it places holds on the relevant records and suspends lifecycle expiration for them, so routine deletion cannot become the destruction that 18 U.S.C. 1519 criminalises.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-4.d`](#us-sec-17a-4-d), [`us-sox-802.1519`](#us-sox-802-1519)
- **Evidence:**
  - Legal-hold register listing each matter, its scope, the date the hold was placed, and who authorised it
  - S3 object metadata showing ObjectLockLegalHoldStatus ON for held objects
  - CloudTrail events for PutObjectLegalHold, showing who placed and removed each hold
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon S3 Object Lock legal hold](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html): Legal hold ON for life-of-enterprise classes and for records in scope of an active matter
- **Limits:** The technical hold only works if the procedure is triggered in time. Knowing when a matter is contemplated is a legal judgement, not something the platform decides.

<a id="ctl-integrity-verification"></a>

### Automated verification of storage completeness and accuracy

`ctl-integrity-verification` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Upload every record with an S3 additional checksum computed by the producer. Reconcile on a schedule: compare the producing system's record manifest with S3 Inventory (completeness), and recompute stored checksums against the manifest (accuracy). Alert on any gap.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-4.f2ii`](#us-sec-17a-4-f2ii), [`us-cftc-1-31.c2`](#us-cftc-1-31-c2)
- **Evidence:**
  - Scheduled reconciliation reports comparing expected and stored record counts and checksums, retained with the records
  - Alarm history for reconciliation failures and their resolution
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon S3 additional checksums](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/checking-object-integrity.html): SHA-256 checksum supplied on upload and stored with each object
  - [Amazon S3 Inventory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-inventory.html): Inventory including checksum algorithm, feeding the reconciliation job

<a id="ctl-records-register"></a>

### Register of required records, their producing systems and locations

`ctl-records-register` · organizational · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Maintain a register that maps each record type the rules require to its producing system, owner, retention class and storage location, plus the index keys needed to find any single record. Generate a searchable index (record id, class, dates, account, S3 key) from S3 Inventory and object metadata, queryable with Athena. The same register is the up-to-date system inventory that CFTC 1.31(c)(2)(iii) requires.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-3.a`](#us-sec-17a-3-a), [`us-sec-17a-3.a6`](#us-sec-17a-3-a6), [`us-finra-4511.a`](#us-finra-4511-a), [`us-sec-17a-4.f3iv`](#us-sec-17a-4-f3iv), [`us-sec-204-2.g2`](#us-sec-204-2-g2), [`us-cftc-1-31.c2`](#us-cftc-1-31-c2)
- **Evidence:**
  - The register, versioned, reviewed at least as often as this corpus's review cycle
  - Athena query results locating sample records on request, kept as test evidence
  - AWS Config resource inventory for the systems named in the register
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon Athena over S3 Inventory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/what-is.html): Tables over inventory and metadata exports providing the locate-any-record index
  - [AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/resource-config-reference.html): Resource inventory of the systems in the register

<a id="ctl-redundant-copy"></a>

### Separately stored, locked redundant copy

`ctl-redundant-copy` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Back up the records buckets with AWS Backup to a vault in a separate AWS account, with Vault Lock in compliance mode and a minimum retention of at least the longest period in the retention schedule. Keep the copy in the project's designated region unless a second region has been deliberately approved. The separation that matters here is account and credential isolation, which protects against the loss of the primary system.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-4.f2v`](#us-sec-17a-4-f2v), [`us-sec-204-2.g2iii`](#us-sec-204-2-g2iii), [`us-cftc-1-31.c2`](#us-cftc-1-31-c2)
- **Evidence:**
  - Backup plan and vault configuration showing Vault Lock in compliance mode and its minimum retention
  - Restore-test records proving the copy can serve as the redundant set
- **AWS:**
  - [AWS Backup Vault Lock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/vault-lock.html): Compliance-mode vault lock in a dedicated backup account; minimum retention at least the longest scheduled period

<a id="ctl-regulator-production"></a>

### Tested procedure for producing records to regulators

`ctl-regulator-production` · organizational · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Keep a production runbook covering the request, the locate query against the records register, export in both human-readable and reasonably usable electronic formats with any audit trail, and delivery. Run it on a schedule against sampled records and time each run, so that "promptly" is backed by evidence. The same path serves client requests for MiFID II recordings.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-4.j`](#us-sec-17a-4-j), [`us-sec-17a-4.f3iv`](#us-sec-17a-4-f3iv), [`us-sec-204-2.g2`](#us-sec-204-2-g2), [`us-cftc-1-31.d3`](#us-cftc-1-31-d3)
- **Evidence:**
  - The runbook and the dated results of each production drill, including elapsed time
  - Delivered production packages and their manifests
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon S3 Batch Operations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/batch-ops.html): Bulk copy of located records and audit-trail extracts into a production bucket

<a id="ctl-regulatory-undertakings"></a>

### Executive and third-party undertakings for electronic records

`ctl-regulatory-undertakings` · organizational · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

File the 17a-4(f)(3)(v) undertaking with the designated examining authority, signed by a designated executive officer (who may appoint designated officers and specialists) or by a designated third party. For records held in a cloud provider's storage, either obtain the provider's full 17a-4(i)(1)(i) undertaking, or establish and document independent access. Independent access means the firm can reach, examine and furnish the records without the provider's intervention, which makes the shorter 17a-4(i)(1)(ii) undertaking available.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-4.f3v`](#us-sec-17a-4-f3v), [`us-sec-17a-4.i`](#us-sec-17a-4-i)
- **Evidence:**
  - Filed undertakings, with the date and recipient of each filing
  - Written appointments of designated officers and specialists
  - An independent-access test showing the firm retrieving and producing records using only its own credentials
- **Limits:** No AWS configuration satisfies this control. It is a filing and a governance act that the firm must perform.

<a id="ctl-retention-schedule"></a>

### Retention schedule mapping record classes to periods and triggers

`ctl-retention-schedule` · organizational · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Keep a retention schedule, generated from this corpus's export, that assigns every record class a period, a trigger and an accessibility window. Put fixed-from-creation classes in buckets whose default retention equals the period. Trigger-based classes (account closure, end of fiscal year, transaction termination, end of the enterprise) cannot know their end date at write time. Write them with the minimum known retention, then extend the retain-until date when the trigger event occurs. Compliance mode allows extending a retention period but never shortening it. Where regimes overlap, take the longest applicable period.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-4.a`](#us-sec-17a-4-a), [`us-sec-17a-4.b`](#us-sec-17a-4-b), [`us-sec-17a-4.c`](#us-sec-17a-4-c), [`us-sec-204-2.e1`](#us-sec-204-2-e1), [`us-sec-204-2.e2`](#us-sec-204-2-e2), [`us-finra-4511.b`](#us-finra-4511-b), [`us-cftc-1-31.b1`](#us-cftc-1-31-b1), [`us-cftc-1-31.b2`](#us-cftc-1-31-b2), [`us-cftc-1-31.b3`](#us-cftc-1-31-b3), [`us-cftc-1-31.b4`](#us-cftc-1-31-b4), [`us-sox-802.1520`](#us-sox-802-1520), [`us-sox-802.rule2-06`](#us-sox-802-rule2-06)
- **Evidence:**
  - The retention schedule, versioned, with each row citing an obligation id from this corpus
  - S3 Inventory reports showing each object's retain-until date against the schedule
  - Records of the jobs that extend retention on trigger events, for example S3 Batch Operations manifests and completion reports
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon S3 Object Lock retention periods](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html): Bucket default retention per record class; per-object retain-until dates extended on trigger events
    <br>*AWS documentation:* “When an object is locked in compliance mode, its retention mode can't be changed, and its retention period can't be shortened.”
  - [Amazon S3 Batch Operations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/batch-ops.html): Bulk retain-until extension when a trigger event (for example account closure) fires
  - [Amazon S3 Inventory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-inventory.html): Daily inventory including Object Lock retain-until date and mode
- **Limits:** The corpus carries the regulatory floor only. Litigation, tax and client-contract retention can exceed it and must be added to the schedule separately.

<a id="ctl-worm-storage"></a>

### Non-rewriteable, non-erasable record storage

`ctl-worm-storage` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Write regulatory records only to S3 buckets created with Object Lock enabled and a default retention in compliance mode. Compliance mode is the WORM option in Rule 17a-4(f)(2)(i)(B). Governance mode is not, because privileged users can bypass it. Enable versioning (Object Lock requires it) so that a correction is written as a new version and the prior content survives, which is what Delegated Regulation 2017/565 Article 72(1)(b) asks for.

- **Satisfies here:** [`us-sec-17a-4.f2i`](#us-sec-17a-4-f2i), [`us-finra-4511.c`](#us-finra-4511-c), [`us-sec-204-2.g3`](#us-sec-204-2-g3), [`us-cftc-1-31.c2`](#us-cftc-1-31-c2)
- **Evidence:**
  - Bucket ObjectLockConfiguration showing ObjectLockEnabled and a DefaultRetention in COMPLIANCE mode
  - AWS Config rule s3-bucket-default-lock-enabled reporting COMPLIANT for every records bucket
  - The Cohasset Associates compliance assessment of S3 Object Lock that AWS links from its documentation, filed with the control evidence
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon S3 Object Lock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html): Object Lock enabled at bucket creation; default retention mode COMPLIANCE; versioning on
    <br>*AWS documentation:* “S3 Object Lock has been assessed by Cohasset Associates for use in environments that are subject to SEC 17a-4, CFTC, and FINRA regulations.”
  - [AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-bucket-default-lock-enabled.html): Managed rule s3-bucket-default-lock-enabled scoped to the records buckets
- **Limits:** The Cohasset assessment covers the storage layer only. The firm still owns the retention schedule, the audit system for inputs under 17a-4(f)(3)(iii), and the undertakings.
